_doc: Napoléon · epilogue: from the will (Longwood, 1821), to his son. French = modern spelling (obvious slips and old spellings corrected without marks in the app); each message keeps the printed text in orig.fr (data only, not shown). en · ko translated from the French for this app. Sexual lines and battle reports are left out (see excerpt). Replies and talks are written by this app, not by the recipients.

hint.ko: 바람 뒤 que 절은 접속법 · je désire que mes cendres reposent, je veux que tu sois heureux, que tu reviennes · VII.0 복습
hint.en: After a wish, the que clause is subjunctive · je désire que mes cendres reposent, que tu reviennes · review of VII.0

hint.ko: 이루어질 수 있는 바람은 hope + 현재 · 미래, 아쉬운 바람은 wish + 과거 · I hope you come back. I wish you were here.
hint.en: A wish that can come true: hope + present/future; a regretful one: wish + past · I hope you come back. I wish you were here.

hint.ko: 윗사람이 아랫사람에게 하는 옛 말투의 명령 · 잊지 말거라, 잘 있거라 · 지금은 -아/어라 (잊지 마라), 높이면 -(으)세요
hint.en: An old-fashioned command from an elder · 잊지 말거라, 잘 있거라 · today -아/어라 (잊지 마라); politely -(으)세요

hint.ko: 부정법을 부정할 때는 ne 와 jamais 가 둘 다 동사 앞 · je te demande de ne jamais oublier · ne pas 도 같아요 (de ne pas partir)
hint.en: With an infinitive, ne and jamais both go before the verb · de ne jamais oublier · the same with ne pas (de ne pas partir)

hint.ko: 부탁 · 당부를 옮길 때 · He asked me never to forget. · not · never 는 to 앞 (to not 은 입말)
hint.en: Passing on a request · He asked me never to forget. · not / never goes before to (‘to not’ is informal)

hint.ko: ‘-지 마’ 를 남에게 옮길 때 · 잊지 말라고 하셨어요 · VII.2 -(으)라고 했어요 복습 · ‘마라고’ 는 틀린 꼴
hint.en: Reporting a ‘don't’ · 잊지 말라고 하셨어요 (he told me not to forget) · review of VII.2 · not ‘마라고’

name.ko: devoir + 부정법 (il doit · il ne doit jamais)
name.en: devoir + infinitive (il doit, il ne doit jamais)

hint.ko: ‘~해야 한다 · 절대 ~하면 안 된다’ · il doit adopter, il ne doit jamais combattre · ne … jamais 는 devoir 를 감싸요
hint.en: ‘must’ / ‘must never’ · il doit adopter, il ne doit jamais combattre · ne … jamais goes around devoir

hint.ko: 강한 의무 · 금지 · He must never fight. · 뒤에는 동사원형 · VI.0 복습
hint.en: Strong duty or ban · He must never fight. · followed by the base verb · review of VI.0

hint.ko: 해야 할 일과 하면 안 되는 일 · 기억해야 해요, 싸우면 안 돼요 · VI.0 복습
hint.en: What you must and must not do · 기억해야 해요, 싸우면 안 돼요 · review of VI.0

messages.fr: Je désire que mes cendres reposent sur les bords de la Seine, au milieu de ce peuple français que j'ai tant aimé.
messages.en: I wish my ashes to rest on the banks of the Seine, among the French people whom I have loved so much.

messages.fr: J'ai toujours eu à me louer de ma très chère épouse Marie-Louise ; je lui conserve jusqu'au dernier moment les plus tendres sentiments. Je la prie de veiller pour garantir mon fils des embûches qui environnent encore son enfance.
messages.en: I have always had reason to be pleased with my dearest wife Marie-Louise; I keep for her, to the very last moment, the tenderest feelings. I ask her to watch over my son and keep him from the traps that still surround his childhood.
messages.ko: 나의 소중한 아내 마리 루이즈에게 나는 늘 고마웠다. 마지막 순간까지 그녀에게 가장 다정한 마음을 간직한다. 아직 어린 내 아들을 둘러싼 함정들로부터 아들을 지켜 주기를 그녀에게 부탁한다.

messages.fr: Je recommande à mon fils de ne jamais oublier qu'il est né prince français, et de ne jamais se prêter à être un instrument entre les mains des triumvirs qui oppriment les peuples de l'Europe.
messages.en: I urge my son never to forget that he was born a French prince, and never to let himself become a tool in the hands of the triumvirs who oppress the peoples of Europe.

note.ko: 워털루 전투 뒤 영국은 나폴레옹을 남대서양 한가운데의 섬 세인트헬레나로 보냈어요. 1821년 4월, 병이 깊어진 그는 롱우드에서 유언장을 썼고, 3주 뒤인 5월 5일 쉰한 살로 숨을 거두었어요. 이 글은 편지가 아니라 유언장 가운데 아들에게 남긴 대목이에요. ‘세 나라 권력자들(triumvirs)’ 은 그를 무너뜨린 동맹국들을 가리켜요. 아들(로마 왕, 훗날 라이히슈타트 공)은 그때 열 살로 빈의 외가에 있었고, 1832년 스물한 살에 세상을 떠나요. ‘센 강가에 잠들고 싶다’ 는 바람은 1840년 유해가 파리의 앵발리드로 돌아오면서 이루어졌어요. 유언장의 한국어는 유언 글말(-다)로 옮겼어요.
note.en: After Waterloo the British sent Napoleon to St Helena, an island in the middle of the South Atlantic. In April 1821, gravely ill, he wrote his will at Longwood; three weeks later, on 5 May, he died at fifty-one. This is not a letter but the passages of his will that speak to and about his son. The ‘triumvirs’ are the allied powers that brought him down. The son (the King of Rome, later Duke of Reichstadt) was ten, living with his mother's family in Vienna; he died in 1832 at twenty-one. The wish to rest ‘on the banks of the Seine’ came true in 1840, when his remains were brought back to the Invalides in Paris.
note.source: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, publiée par ordre de l'empereur Napoléon III, Paris, Imprimerie impériale / Plon-Dumaine, 1858-1870, t. XXXII (1870), 'Œuvres de Napoléon Ier à Sainte-Hélène', Testament, pp. 476-477 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/correspondancedeNNnapouoft [identifiant du tome à confirmer] ; image: see plate.imageSource

replies.fr: Papa, je te promets de ne jamais oublier.
replies.en: Dad, you asked me never to forget, and I won't.
replies.ko: 아버지가 잊지 말라고 하셨죠. 절대 안 잊을게요.
replies.koLow: 아버지가 잊지 말라고 했지. 절대 안 잊을게.
replies.koHigh: 아버지께서 잊지 말라고 하셨지요. 절대 잊지 않겠습니다.

replies.fr: Moi aussi, je désire que tu reviennes un jour en France.
replies.en: I hope you come back to France one day too.

replies.fr: Je dois garder ta devise, et je ne dois jamais faire de mal à la France.
replies.en: I must keep your motto, and I must never harm France.

options.en: On the banks of the Seine

scene.en: An imagined call: the ten-year-old son in Vienna and his father on St Helena

lines.fr: Bonjour, mon fils. Tu travailles bien à l'école ?
lines.en: Hello, son. Are you working hard at school?
lines.ko: 안녕, 아들. 공부는 열심히 하고 있니?

lines.fr: Oui, papa. J'apprends le français et l'histoire.
lines.en: Yes, Dad. I'm learning French and history.
lines.ko: 네, 아버지. 프랑스어랑 역사를 배우고 있어요.

lines.fr: Très bien. N'oublie jamais : tu es né prince français.
lines.en: Very good. Never forget: you were born a French prince.
lines.ko: 잘했다. 잊지 말거라. 너는 프랑스 왕자로 태어났단다.

lines.fr: Je ne l'oublierai jamais, papa. C'est promis.
lines.en: I'll never forget it, Dad. I promise.
